key_findings: Dry-bulb T fits cooling-season campus load BETTER than WBGT/HI/T_app (R²: T=0.22 > HI=0.19 > T_app=0.18 > WBGT=0.16). Interpretation: in low-humidity-variation summer with metered total load, dry-bulb T already captures most signal.
Calendar modulation PERSISTS under WBGT: class-day cooling slope 36.7, weekend 24.1 (×1.52), R² 0.91 vs 0.81. Confirms the calendar effect is occupant-driven, not a humidity confound.

Balance-point temperature gap of 4.0°C across day_types (授業日 18.4 / 週末 19.3 / 休業 22.4). Building-physics interpretation: ΔT_balance = ΔQ_internal/UA. The 4°C gap quantifies occupant internal heat gain difference.
Same-WBGT load excess on class days: at WBGT 28-29°C, class days draw 307 kWh/h more than weekends. This is direct evidence of occupant + equipment + lighting internal gains, independent of weather.
